recordedOn: Apple M4 Max, macOS 26.5.2, Node 22.23.1 (the flake devShell's node -- the version CI runs; recorded with `nix develop --command pnpm bench`). Each figure is the median of TEN whole-benchmark runs. Interquartile spread was 3.3-7.5% for guards and 3.6-8.6% for workloads; the machine was lightly loaded, unlike the previous recording. See the note.
note: guards are slow/fast A/B ratios measured in one process against one data set: the machine cancels, so these are the real gate (tolerance 1.30, except the shipped-vs-frozen gate at 1.15). workloads are workload/yardstick ratios and are only approximately machine-independent -- indicative, not authoritative (tolerance 2.0). WHAT MOVED IN THIS RECORDING, AND WHY: one feature landed -- FLUID SURFACE MESHING (domain/fluid-mesh.ts, docs/design-notes.md M-12). A fluid block is skipped by the six cube passes and its surface is emitted instead as a bilinear patch with four independent corner heights, which CANNOT be merged, so it is counted in neither totalQuadArea nor totalQuadCount. TWO NEW WORKLOAD ENTRIES, and they are a pair: meshChunk/lake-fluid and meshChunk/lake-as-cubes run the SAME chunk bytes under two configs, one declaring water a fluid and one not. lake-fluid is 11.677 against lake-as-cubes 6.080, i.e. 1.92x, and the quad figures say why -- 35 merged water quads become 1,056 unmergeable 1x1 patches. That is the list price of a stepped water surface, not a regression: a surface with per-corner heights and a surface that merges into rectangles are mutually exclusive. mc-render may decline to pass fluidMaxLevels for distant chunks and get the cube behaviour back. THE FOUR ORIGINAL FIXTURES DID NOT MOVE and were not expected to: none of them declares a fluid, so meshChunk/* lands at 1.01-1.06x of the previous recording and meshChunkNaive/* at 0.93-1.01x, all inside this recording's own spread. simplifyMesh/* is unmoved (0.97-1.04x); nothing in the feature touches it. GUARDS DID NOT MOVE: all five land within 0.93-1.03x. WHAT A FLUID-FREE CONFIG PAYS, AND WHY THE NUMBER IS NOT HERE: two things were added to that path -- one byte-table read in the six passes' guard, and the meshFluidSurfaces call itself. The second is defused by a 256-byte early exit (without it a fluid-free config pays a whole extra 16 x yLimit x 16 walk). The first was measured by interleaved paired runs, 5 pairs, pre-feature against shipped: 1.00-1.08x on meshChunk and 0.98-1.04x on meshChunkNaive, against per-arm spreads of 5.5-10.9%. THAT IS NOT A RESULT -- the effect is the same size as the noise and one row came out below 1.0. What can be said is that no charge above roughly 1.1x was observed. M-11 could report 1.08x for the plant read because that pairing was less buried; this one cannot make a claim of that strength and does not. ON SPREAD: across the ten recording runs the interquartile spread was 3.3-7.5% for guards and 3.6-8.6% for workloads -- much tighter than the previous recording's 7.5-31.7% and 6.5-63.0%, because this machine was not under the concurrent load that one was. Figures here are therefore better sampled than the ones they replace, which is worth knowing before treating a small difference against the OLD baseline as signal. ON NODE VERSIONS: the same benchmark on Node 24.13.0 puts the workload ratios well above these. The recorded environment is Node 22; comparing across major versions is not meaningful. Regenerate with `pnpm bench --update-baseline` and say in the commit message what moved and why -- note that a single --update-baseline run records ONE sample, and the figures below are medians of TEN whole-benchmark runs assembled deliberately, as the previous recording also was.
